text: Then, on the night before she left. <break time="0.8s" /> While she was packing up. <break time="0.8s" /> In her grandmothers house on Nuns Island. <break time="0.8s" /> She suddenly heard gravel. <break time="0.8s" /> Thrown up against the window of her room. <break time="0.8s" /> The window was so wet with rain. <break time="0.8s" /> That she could not see out. <break time="0.8s" /> So she ran downstairs as she was and slipped out the back. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the garden. <break time="0.8s" /> Where the poor boy stood shivering at the end. <break time="0.8s" /> She begged him to go home at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Warning him. <break time="0.8s" /> That he would get his death in the rain. <break time="0.8s" /> But he only said. <break time="0.8s" /> That he did not want to live. <break time="0.8s" /> Even now, she cried. <break time="0.8s" /> She could see his eyes as well as well. <break time="0.8s" /> And she remembered. <break time="0.8s" /> How he had stood at the end of the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> Where there was a tree. <break time="0.8s" /> In the rain. <break time="0.8s" /> Scarcely had she spent a week. <break time="0.8s" /> At the convent in Dublin. <break time="0.8s" /> When news came. <break time="0.8s" /> That Michael Furey had died. <break time="0.8s" /> And had been buried in Oughterard. <break time="0.8s" /> Where his people came from. <break time="0.8s" /> Choking with sobs. <break time="0.8s" /> She broke off. <break time="0.8s" /> And, overcome by emotion. <break time="0.8s" /> Flung herself face downward on the bed. <break time="0.8s" /> While Gabriel held her hand a moment longer. <break time="0.8s" /> Uncertain what he should do. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, shy of intruding on her grief. <break time="0.8s" /> He let her hand fall gently. <break time="0.8s" /> And walked quietly to the window. <break time="0.8s" /> And by the time he turned. <break time="0.8s" /> To look at her again. <break time="0.8s" /> She was fast asleep.
